items.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: b1cca82d / aec2b76a / 25ddacc0 'fix(runtime): liveness-guard pinned hook execPath so mise/asdf/nvm Node upgrades don't break hooks (#841)'. ORIGINAL_INTENT (quoted from commit subject): pin the hook command to the resolved execPath specifically so that mise/asdf/nvm node version switches do not silently break hooks after a Node upgrade. v2's row #1090 demands the OPPOSITE for plugin.json under Homebrew: 'command is node (not process.execPath)'.
items.regressions: REGRESSION_RISK (blocker-class): #1090's fix (always write bare 'node') directly conflicts with #841's fix (pin execPath so version-manager upgrades don't break hooks). Applying #1090 literally re-breaks #841 for mise/asdf/nvm users; keeping #841's pinned path re-breaks #1090 for Homebrew-node users whose pinned path becomes stale after brew upgrade.
items.question: Can the install write a path that is resolved lazily at hook-run time (e.g. a tiny shim or `command -v node` fallback) so it survives BOTH a version-manager switch (#841) and a Homebrew upgrade (#1090), instead of picking one pinned string?
items.recommendation: SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: do not just replace process.execPath with the literal string 'node' (that regresses #841). Resolve the binary at hook invocation time (liveness-guard already does something like this for #841) rather than writing a fixed string into plugin.json at install time. ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2's #1090 line ('stable launcher resolved at run time') already points this direction and should be the stated verdict, not a flat rewrite to 'node'.

cross_cutting_findings.finding: ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r2.md contains unfilled template rows (verbatim boilerplate 'Assign each to a GP case (GP3/GP4/GP5/GP11) or to a kept v1 test file, or mark wont-fix with reason') for #1075 and other rows in this half, rather than an actual per-issue verdict. These should not be treated as settled.

#1090 and #841 are a direct, unresolved regression pair: the v2 ask (write bare 'node') and the v1 fix (pin resolved execPath) solve different environments (Homebrew vs version managers) with opposite mechanisms. Needs its own ADR line, not a one-line contract test.

ADR-0008's blanket 'heal scripts removed' does not distinguish install-time cache/marketplace heal (safe to remove per D2) from mid-session sqlite corruption self-heal (db-base withRetry), which covers different historical bugs (#699, #795/#805 vs #1105/#564-class SIGSEGV). The ADR text should name which heal layer is being removed.
